name: Ghostline ThinSkin Grip Infiltration Glove
description:
Ultra-thin second-skin gloves designed for close-access work. The outer surface is micro-textured gecko-polymer — nearly invisible grip enhancement that reads as bare skin to casual inspection but adheres to glass, polished metal, and composite surfaces with unsettling confidence. Interior surface is lined with a biometric-scatter membrane that disrupts fingerprint, palm-vein, and thermal imaging capture at contact points.

Five-finger cut with no reinforcement bulk. Available in twelve skin-tone variants and two synthetic-skin finishes. Tears easily if snagged — designed to be worn as a consumable, not a long-term tool. Sold in packs of three pairs, vacuum-sealed.
functionality: Gecko-polymer surface enhances grip on smooth vertical and inverted surfaces. Biometric-scatter membrane disrupts fingerprint, palm-vein, and thermal imaging at contact. Worn as a consumable — single-use recommended for high-stakes work. Twelve skin-tone variants for visual concealment against the wearer's hands.
what_it_says: You were never here, and if you were, you didn't touch anything.
story_hooks: A torn fragment of a Ghostline glove is found adhered to a 40th-floor window ledge — the biometric scatter membrane is still intact, meaning whoever left it behind hasn't been identified yet.
A new batch of Ghostline skins is circulating with a manufacturing defect: the scatter membrane has a narrow frequency gap that a specific CorpSec scanner model can read through.
A Tier 4 executive is quietly buying Ghostline packs in bulk — not for infiltration, but because they're terrified someone is using them to move through their own secured floor.

physical_description.visual_profile: Nearly invisible second-skin gloves that appear as bare hands at casual distance. Only the subtle micro-texture and slight iridescent shimmer at certain angles betray their presence. Gives wearer an uncanny, almost too-smooth appearance that reads as unsettling to trained observers.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight, hugging every contour of the hand without bulk. Five-finger design with no padding or reinforcement. Seams are virtually undetectable; edges fuse seamlessly with skin tone.
physical_description.primary_material: Gecko-polymer outer surface with biometric-scatter membrane lining. Designed as consumable-grade synthetic with minimal durability.
physical_description.texture: Outer surface is micro-textured at nano-scale, appearing smooth to the naked eye but providing molecular grip. Inner surface is membrane-soft with scattered metallic disruption points. Overall feel is like a second dermis.
physical_description.color_scheme: Twelve human skin-tone variants ranging from deep brown through pale ivory, plus two synthetic-skin finishes (matte chrome-gray and translucent pearl). Available in current batch: warm caramel, cool ash, rich mahogany, pale rose.
physical_description.closures: Friction-fit only; gloves slip on like a second layer of skin with no visible fasteners, seams, or closures.
distinctive_features: Gecko-polymer grip adheres to glass, polished metal, and composites without suction devices
Biometric-scatter membrane disrupts fingerprint and thermal imaging at contact points
Designed as tear-prone consumable — single-use to limited multi-use
Sold vacuum-sealed in packs of three pairs
Twelve skin-tone match variants suggest intentional infiltration use-case
No visible branding; Ghostline label only on packaging
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 street-operation tool. Too specialized and deliberately ungoverned for legal retail. Prices on underground markets: 180-220 Φ per three-pack.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals infiltration specialist, data thief, or sub-grade operative. Wearing these visibly marks you as someone prepared for close-access work — corporate espionage, secure facility breach, or black-market acquisition. Corpo security would flag this immediately.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn condition shows small tears at fingertips and stress points along the knuckle. Biometric-scatter membrane begins visibly degrading after 3-5 uses. Users expect consumable lifespan of 1-3 shifts before disposal.

The glove is so thin it reads as bare skin until the light hits the gecko-polymer grip, revealing an uncanny shimmer. Dark urban warehouse backdrop with security lattice visible behind.
